blockAssessments.assessment: The unit definition concerns charge and potential increments for a fixed isolated-conductor geometry/environment and unchanged potential reference. The underlying electrostatic proportional relation is used within the linear ideal-conductor model. One farad is one coulomb per volt. The historical electrostatic capacitance unit called centimetre is tied to a vacuum isolated sphere, not to an assertion that SI capacitance is a length.

Original equality atoms are retained exactly, while the immediately preceding prose identifies the historical rounded conversion values. Dividing the rounded charge-unit factor3e9 by voltage factor1/300 yields9e11 historical centimetre units per farad. It is not described as an exact modern metrological conversion.

The large physical radius comparison is explicitly limited to an isolated vacuum conducting sphere, not to practical capacitors. The original13-plus historical comparison is marked as an approximate source-era estimate, not a precise contemporary astronomical ratio; the modern constants produce about12.92solar radii, confirming its order of magnitude. Microfarad/picofarad exponents are exact.709microfarads is explicitly a source estimate for an ideal isolated Earth-sized sphere, not an environment-independent measurement.

The rearrangement of source8-34 is restricted to the spherical conductor in a homogeneous linear isotropic medium, with relative permittivity dimensionless and the sphere radius in the denominator. Hence epsilon0 has units F/m and is not a geometry-dependent constant. The source formula retains its complete original TeX atom, including source punctuation; no arbitrary-conductor shape formula is invented.
